title: IRFC Share Price: Decoding its 5-Year Potential
description: IRFC is the dedicated financing arm for Indian Railways, funding rolling stock and infrastructure projects. The company recently reported a 10.21% year-on-yea.

faq.a: IRFC is the dedicated financing arm of Indian Railways. Its main business involves raising funds from domestic and international markets to finance the acquisition of rolling stock (locomotives, coaches, wagons) and railway infrastructure projects, which are then leased to Indian Railways.

faq.q: How does IRFC maintain zero NPAs?
faq.a: IRFC's business model is inherently low-risk because its primary borrower is the Indian Railways, backed by the Government of India. This sovereign guarantee ensures timely repayments, allowing IRFC to maintain a record of zero non-performing assets.

faq.q: What are the key risks associated with investing in IRFC?
faq.a: While IRFC benefits from sovereign backing, key risks include high client concentration (almost exclusive reliance on Indian Railways), sensitivity to interest rate fluctuations affecting borrowing costs, and potential changes in government policy towards railway financing.

faq.q: Has IRFC declared any recent dividends?
faq.a: Yes, for Q2 FY27, IRFC's board approved an interim dividend of ₹1.15 per equity share. The record date for this dividend was October 23, 2026.

faq.q: How does IRFC plan to grow its business?
faq.a: IRFC is strategically focused on diversifying its lending portfolio beyond traditional railway financing. It aims to venture into the broader railway ecosystem and railway-linked infrastructure projects to enhance growth and potentially improve lending margins.
IRFC typically enjoys strong credit ratings, including AAA, due to its sovereign ownership and predictable cash flows, which enables it to borrow funds at competitive rates.

faq.q: What is the significance of IRFC's 'Navratna' status?
faq.a: IRFC was granted 'Navratna' status in March 2025. This status provides greater operational and financial autonomy to the public sector enterprise, potentially allowing it more flexibility in strategic decisions and expansion initiatives.
